title: Mechanical, durability, and microstructural performance of concrete incorporating eggshell powder, coconut shell, and recycled concrete aggregate
content:
Abstract

This study investigates the incorporation of eggshell powder (EP), coconut shell (CS), and recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) in M20 concrete through a sequential three-stage experimental programme involving 13 mixtures. EP replaced cement at 5–15%, CS replaced natural coarse aggregate at 5–30% with 10% EP, and RCA was incorporated at 10–30% with 10% EP and 10% CS. At 28 days, 5% EP achieved the highest compressive strength (26.80 MPa), exceeding the control (26.20 MPa) by 2.3%. Increasing CS reduced strength, although the 10% EP–10% CS mixture retained 98.1% of the control strength. The mixture containing 10% EP, 10% CS, and 30% RCA retained approximately 90% of the control mechanical strength. At 90 days, the mixture containing 10% EP, 10% CS, and 30% RCA exhibited an 8.4% increase in water absorption (2.70% versus 2.49%) and an 8.4% increase in RCPT charge passed (1956 C versus 1804 C), compared with the control. Distinct differences are seen in morphology and ITZ by SEM results. Statistical significance in differences in 28-day compressive strength across EP, CS and RAC mixes is confirmed through Pearson correlation analysis and stage-wise one-way ANOVA. Concrete from the three waste-derived materials showed better mechanical and durability trade-offs, identifying replacement combinations that retain substantial mechanical performance within the investigated ranges.
